name: Loch Lomond & the Trossachs
tagline: Scotland's first national park, a genuinely accessible first taste of the Highlands within easy reach of Glasgow.

shortDescription: Scotland's first national park, home to Loch Lomond, Ben Lomond and the wooded hills of the Trossachs, an easy first taste of the Highlands from Glasgow.

intro: Loch Lomond and the Trossachs is genuinely Scotland's first national park, and for good reason a favourite easy escape from Glasgow, offering a real first taste of Highland scenery within an hour's drive of the city.

Loch Lomond itself is genuinely Britain's largest lake by surface area, its southern shores gentle and accessible, its northern reaches narrowing into properly dramatic Highland terrain around Ben Lomond.

Most visitors genuinely combine a loch cruise or lakeside walk with time in the wooded Trossachs further east, where Loch Katrine's historic steamship and the area's genuinely inspired Sir Walter Scott's romantic writing about the Highlands.

whyVisit.intro: Loch Lomond and the Trossachs' case rests on genuinely offering real Highland scenery within easy reach of Glasgow.

points.title: It's genuinely Scotland's first national park
points.text: Established in 2002, protecting some of the country's most accessible Highland scenery.

points.title: Loch Lomond is genuinely Britain's largest lake by area
points.text: A real sense of scale, especially from the water on a loch cruise.

points.title: Ben Lomond is genuinely an achievable first Munro
points.text: One of the most accessible of Scotland's mountains over 3,000 feet for a first serious hike.

points.title: The Trossachs genuinely inspired Sir Walter Scott
points.text: His writing about the area helped popularise the wider romantic image of the Highlands.

points.title: It's genuinely an easy day trip or overnight from Glasgow
points.text: Under an hour's drive, making it accessible even on a short trip.

attractionsIntro: The park's essential sights combine Loch Lomond's accessible scale with the Trossachs' more intimate, wooded scenery.

attractions.name: Loch Lomond

image.alt: Loch Lomond, Britain's largest lake by surface area

attractions.text: Genuinely Britain's largest lake by surface area, its southern shores gentle and its northern reaches narrowing into dramatic Highland terrain.
attractions.tip: Genuinely the loch's character changes dramatically from south to north — see both if time allows.

attractions.name: Ben Lomond
attractions.text: Genuinely one of Scotland's most accessible Munros, a mountain over 3,000 feet, with sweeping views over the loch from the summit.
attractions.tip: The genuinely standard route takes four to six hours round trip and needs no technical climbing.

attractions.name: Luss village

image.alt: The village of Luss on the shore of Loch Lomond

attractions.text: Genuinely one of Scotland's prettiest lochside villages, its stone cottages and pier a popular, easy stop on the loch's western shore.
attractions.tip: Genuinely arrive early or late to avoid the busiest midday tour bus crowds.

attractions.name: Loch Katrine

image.alt: Loch Katrine in the heart of the Trossachs

attractions.text: Genuinely the scenic heart of the Trossachs, a loch that helped inspire Sir Walter Scott's romantic writing about the Highlands.
attractions.tip: The genuinely surrounding forest offers excellent, easy cycling and walking trails.

attractions.name: The SS Sir Walter Scott

image.file: File:SS Sir Walter Scott At Trossachs Pier - geograph.org.uk - 4431047.jpg
image.alt: The SS Sir Walter Scott steamship on Loch Katrine

attractions.text: Genuinely a historic Victorian steamship, still carrying passengers across Loch Katrine over a century after entering service.
attractions.tip: Genuinely book ahead in summer — it's one of the Trossachs' most popular attractions.

attractions.name: The Trossachs

image.alt: The wooded hills of the Trossachs at sunset

attractions.text: Genuinely a more intimate, wooded landscape than Loch Lomond itself, often called 'the Highlands in miniature.'
attractions.tip: Genuinely a rewarding scenic drive, best taken slowly with several stops.

attractions.name: Loch Lomond near Tarbet

image.alt: Loch Lomond near the village of Tarbet

attractions.text: Genuinely where the loch begins to narrow and turn properly Highland in character, a striking contrast to its wider southern reaches.
attractions.tip: Genuinely a good stop for photos looking north toward the narrower, more dramatic upper loch.

thingsToDoIntro: The park genuinely rewards combining time on the water with a proper walk or hike.

thingsToDo.title: Cruise Loch Lomond

image.alt: A cruise boat on Loch Lomond

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely relaxed way to appreciate the loch's real scale, with regular sailings departing from Balloch and Luss.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely a shorter cruise from Luss covers some of the loch's most scenic stretches.

thingsToDo.title: Hike Ben Lomond

image.file: File:North ridge of Ben Lomond - geograph.org.uk - 3231298.jpg
image.alt: Hiking the ridge of Ben Lomond

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely achievable first Munro for many visitors, rewarded with sweeping summit views over the loch.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely start early and check the weather — conditions change quickly at altitude even here.

thingsToDo.title: Wander Luss village
thingsToDo.text: A genuinely easy, pretty stop, strolling stone cottages and a short pier out onto the loch itself.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely combine with a coffee stop at one of the village's small cafés.

thingsToDo.title: Sail Loch Katrine on the SS Sir Walter Scott

image.file: File:SS Sir Walter Scott at Trossachs Pier - geograph.org.uk - 6857558.jpg
image.alt: Boarding the SS Sir Walter Scott on Loch Katrine

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely memorable way to see the Trossachs, a slow cruise aboard a working Victorian steamship.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely book ahead in peak summer, when sailings can sell out.

thingsToDo.title: Drive through the Trossachs

image.alt: A scenic drive through the Trossachs

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely rewarding, unhurried drive through wooded hills often described as 'the Highlands in miniature.'
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely stop often — the scenery here rewards a slow pace more than covering distance.

thingsToDo.title: Photograph Ellen's Isle on Loch Katrine

image.file: File:Ellen's Isle, Loch Katrine, Trossachs, Scotland-LCCN2002695066.jpg

thingsToDo.text: A genuinely scenic small island, named for the heroine of Sir Walter Scott's poem set on the loch.
thingsToDo.tip: Genuinely best viewed from the SS Sir Walter Scott's regular cruise route.

bestTime.headline: May to September for the best weather, though the park works well year-round
bestTime.summary: Loch Lomond and the Trossachs are genuinely visitable in any season, though hiking and cruising are easiest in the warmer months.

tipsIntro: Practical notes that make a Loch Lomond and Trossachs visit noticeably smoother.
tips: Book genuinely SS Sir Walter Scott sailings ahead in peak summer.
Start genuinely early for Ben Lomond — the trailhead car park fills fast on fine days.
Check genuinely weather conditions before any higher-altitude hike.
Pack a proper waterproof layer regardless of season.
Visit genuinely Luss early or late to avoid the busiest midday tour bus crowds.
Consider genuinely the train to Balloch if visiting without a car.

faq.q: How many days do you need at Loch Lomond and the Trossachs?
faq.a: One to two days genuinely covers Luss, a loch cruise and the Trossachs comfortably.

faq.q: Can you visit as a day trip from Glasgow?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely easily — Balloch is under an hour away by train, making it one of Scotland's most accessible national parks.

faq.q: Is Ben Lomond difficult to climb?
faq.a: Genuinely moderate — it's one of the more accessible Munros, taking four to six hours round trip without requiring technical climbing skill.

faq.q: What is Loch Lomond known for?
faq.a: Genuinely being Britain's largest lake by surface area, and for inspiring the well-known folk song of the same name.

faq.q: Is the SS Sir Walter Scott worth it?
faq.a: Yes, genuinely — it's a historic working Victorian steamship, and a memorable, relaxed way to see Loch Katrine.

faq.q: How far is Loch Lomond from Glasgow?
faq.a: Genuinely very close, under an hour's drive or train ride, making it an easy day trip or short overnight from the city.
